# Takeout Photo

> Takeout Photo is a desktop app for Mac and Windows that runs on your own computer and reads your Google Takeout export in place (.zip and .tgz archives, without unpacking them). It turns your Google Photos into a private timeline of trips, places and maps, matches your photos to your Strava, Komoot or Garmin Connect activities along the GPS track, or moves them to Proton Photos with albums and metadata intact. A Docker image for a NAS runs it on your home network. Everything is processed locally; your photos are never uploaded to our servers.

## Download

- [Download for Mac](https://github.com/ecyshor/takepho.com/releases/latest/download/TakeoutPhoto-macos-arm64.dmg): the latest release as a .dmg. Apple silicon (arm64) only, macOS 12 (Monterey) or later, signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized. The app updates itself (Sparkle; "Check for Updates…" menu, automatic checks can be turned off in Settings → Updates). [Release notes](https://github.com/ecyshor/takepho.com/releases).
- [Download for Windows](https://github.com/ecyshor/takepho.com/releases/latest/download/TakeoutPhoto-windows-x64-setup.exe): the latest release as an installer (.exe); a portable [TakeoutPhoto-windows-x64.zip](https://github.com/ecyshor/takepho.com/releases/latest/download/TakeoutPhoto-windows-x64.zip) is also available. Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit. The Windows app isn't code-signed yet, so the first launch shows "Windows protected your PC" — click "More info", then "Run anyway". The installed app updates itself automatically (checks daily in Settings → Updates and installs when the app quits; updates are EdDSA-verified like the Mac feed), while the portable zip doesn't — new versions are on the [releases page](https://github.com/ecyshor/takepho.com/releases).
- Free to download and explore: the sample library in the app or the [read-only demo](https://takepho.com/demo/). **Lite (free)** imports your own Takeout manually (a local folder of .tgz/.zip archives) and shows your 5 most recent holidays in the photo timeline — no account needed; a paid plan unlocks the whole library (see Pricing).
- Self-host on a NAS: run the Docker image with Docker Compose on your home server or NAS and open it in the browser on your network. See [Self-hosting](https://takepho.com/self-host/).

## Self-hosting on a NAS

- Run the same app — with its built-in Photos timeline, Activities and Proton Photos sync — on your NAS or home server with Docker Compose, in your browser on your network: [Run Takeout Photo on a NAS with Docker Compose](https://takepho.com/self-host/).
- Image: `ghcr.io/ecyshor/takepho:latest` (amd64 and arm64); optional CUDA image `ghcr.io/ecyshor/takepho-cuda:latest` for an NVIDIA GPU. `:latest` always points at the newest release; every release also has a pinned tag, e.g. `ghcr.io/ecyshor/takepho:1.2.0` and `ghcr.io/ecyshor/takepho-cuda:1.2.0`. Requires Docker Engine with Compose v2.24+, an x86-64 or 64-bit ARM CPU and 4 GB RAM free for the container (8 GB recommended for big libraries).
- Same plans and prices as the desktop app, including free Lite (see Pricing); for a paid plan the NAS counts as one of your account's 2 devices, and it needs internet at least once a month to refresh the licence.
- Security: the published compose file turns on Google sign-in (AUTH_ENABLED=true; restrict accounts with AUTH_ALLOWED_EMAILS). Even so, keep it on your home network or behind a VPN, and never forward the port to the internet.

## How it works

1. Request your Takeout at [takeout.google.com](https://takeout.google.com): your export arrives as one or more archive files (takeout-001.zip, ...).
2. Takeout Photo processes it on your computer: it reads .zip/.tgz archives in place without unpacking, from a folder, a Google Drive link, or read-only Google sign-in; it reads the JSON sidecars for the real dates, GPS and descriptions; it handles libraries of hundreds of GB (for a real 249 GB Takeout with about 34,000 photos the app stores about 12.6 GB of thumbnails and previews, a 370 MB index and a 170 MB database; the archives are read in place and never unpacked or copied, 0 GB unpacked, and re-reading the inventory of 233 GB of archives takes about a minute, after the first import); newer exports merge in (with Lite you import a newer export manually, limited to your 5 most recent holidays; incrementally on the yearly plan; rebuild with edits kept on Lifetime). Interrupted work resumes automatically: if the app is closed, the computer restarts or the app updates mid-import or mid-processing, the import and processing pick up where they left off on the next start (already imported items are skipped; an import that stopped has a "Resume import" button; every import shows its steps as a checklist with the current step live). Your photos are never uploaded to our servers.
3. Explore it in Takeout Photo: the built-in Photos timeline, Activities (photos on Strava, Komoot and Garmin Connect activities) and Proton Photos sync. Each one opens for the data your export contains.

## Pricing

- **Lite (free)**: no account or licence needed. Import your own Takeout manually: a local folder of .tgz/.zip archives, including a newer export later. No automatic imports: when you have a new export, add it to your folder and run Import again. Photo timeline only, read-only, limited to your 5 most recent holidays plus the home periods and day trips in that span (the app shows "5 of N holidays"). No Strava/Komoot/Garmin activity matching, no Proton Photos move. Lifetime or Yearly unlocks the whole library — the rest of the photos are processed in the background, without re-importing.
- **Lifetime licence**: one-time USD 25. Import your Takeout manually (folder on disk, a Google Drive link, or read-only Google sign-in); unlocks the whole library with no photo limits (the rest of the photos are processed in the background, without re-importing); importing a newer export rebuilds the library with your edits (hidden photos, trip names/notes, homes, people) kept; all app updates included.
- **Yearly subscription**: USD 25 for the first year, then every renewal is automatically 50% off (USD 12.50 per year). Everything in Lifetime plus automatic processing (folder watcher imports new exports as they land, incremental imports of newer exports without rebuild, contributors such as a partner's Takeout). The first paid year includes the Lifetime licence: if you cancel, you keep it.
- Prices include taxes; the currency is picked from your country at checkout: USD 25 (United States and rest of the world), EUR 20 (Europe), GBP 20 (United Kingdom), CHF 20 (Switzerland and Liechtenstein) — these are the first-year prices, and yearly renewals after the first year are half price (USD 12.50, EUR 10, GBP 10, CHF 10).
- Buy inside the app: Settings → Account, sign in with Google or Apple, choose a plan and pay. Prices include taxes; cancel any time from the app's "Manage subscription" button. One account covers 2 devices (Mac or Windows). The app works offline on a signed entitlement, refreshed about weekly (internet at least once a month).

## FAQ

- **Is there a phone app?** No. Takeout Photo is a desktop app for Mac and Windows. If you run the Docker image on a NAS or home server, you can open it in the browser of any device on your network, including a phone.
- **How much disk space does it need?** The archives themselves, plus a small local library. For a real 249 GB Takeout with about 34,000 photos the app stores about 12.6 GB of thumbnails and previews, a 370 MB index and a 170 MB database. The archives are read in place and never unpacked or copied.
- **Do I need to keep the Takeout archives after importing?** Yes, if you want full-resolution originals. Browsing uses local previews, but originals are read from the archives on demand, so keep them in your folder or on Drive.
- **Can I rename or hide trips?** Yes, with Lifetime or Yearly: rename a trip, add notes, pick its cover, hide trips or photos, and set your homes. Lite is read-only. Your edits are kept when you import a newer export.
- **Does it show videos and HEIC photos?** HEIC photos are decoded on your computer and shown like any other photo. The timeline shows photos today; videos in your Takeout are counted in the inventory and uploaded by the Proton Photos sync.

## What you can do with your Google Photos Takeout

- [Google Photos Takeout viewer: browse your export as a timeline](https://takepho.com/google-photos-takeout/): read the .zip/.tgz archives in place, get the real capture dates and GPS from the JSON sidecar files, and browse trips, places and routes on a map, the timeline as rows or one long scroll by year, trip by trip, or as numbers on the Overview page (countries visited and holiday days per year, plus flights taken and kilometres flown from your Google Maps Timeline). With Lifetime or Yearly you can also rename, annotate and hide trips, set your homes, and keep or remove photos flagged "Deleted in Google Photos".
- [See your Google Photos on your Strava activities](https://takepho.com/google-photos-strava/): sync activities from Strava (official API, OAuth), Komoot or Garmin Connect (your own login) and match your Takeout photos to each activity by capture time, placed along the GPS track ("km 12.3 · 10:42"). All your routes are on one map, coloured by sport, with a heatmap mode, and the Stats page totals distance, time and elevation per year.
- [Move your Google Photos to Proton Photos](https://takepho.com/google-photos-to-proton-photos/): import the Google Photos part of your Takeout into Proton Photos (Proton Drive) in full original quality, with albums or trip albums (trip albums named "{Type} {place} – {Month YYYY}", e.g. "Holiday Alcúdia, Spain – May 2025"), and capture date, GPS, description, favourite and people written losslessly into the files from the Takeout JSON sidecars, uploaded via Proton's official open-source Drive CLI. Pause and resume at any time; an interrupted sync continues on the next start. A sync never deletes anything in your Proton account, and Revert sync moves what the app uploaded to the Proton trash.
- Coming next: more sync destinations beyond Proton Photos, and support for Google Drive and Google Docs files from your Takeout (today only the Google Photos part is used).
- [Home](https://takepho.com/): download, how it works, features, platforms, pricing, FAQ.
- [Read-only demo](https://takepho.com/demo/): try the app in your browser with a sample library.
- [Self-hosting on a NAS](https://takepho.com/self-host/): Docker Compose on your home server or NAS.

## Status

The Mac app (Apple silicon) and the Windows app (Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit) are downloadable now, see Download above. A Docker image for a NAS is available too. A live read-only demo is at https://takepho.com/demo/.

## Privacy

Everything is processed locally on your computer; your photos are never uploaded to our servers. If you sign in with Google, access is read-only and limited to the files you pick. The account service (account.takepho.com, hosted on Hetzner in Germany) stores only your sign-in identity, your purchase records (no card data) and your registered devices (device id, name, last seen); it is backed up nightly (14 days). Full policy: https://takepho.com/privacy.html
